paragraphs: The Clevetura S keyboard stands out due to its dual functionality, which combines a Mac keyboard with a built-in trackpad. The twist is that instead of adding a dedicated trackpad to the keyboard, it turns the keys themselves into a touch surface.
This clever idea works well in daily use, although it comes with a learning curve.

Keyboards for Macs come in all shapes and sizes, from compact models to split designs built for better ergonomics. Some that I’ve tested over the years excelled due to specific features or connectivity options, but almost none of them aim to replace the mouse or trackpad.
That’s what the Clevetura S does. It lets you type, swipe and even use various Mac gestures from the keyboard’s surface.

The Clevetura S turns its keys into a touchpad, letting you trigger macOS gestures without moving your hands away from the keyboard. Customizable touch sliders, backlighting and multiple device connections add versatility, though the design takes getting used to and battery life is modest.

The Clevetura S takes its design cues from Apple’s Magic Keyboard, with white keys and a silver frame. The biggest difference is how closely the keys sit together. There’s a negligible gap between the keycaps on the Clevetura keyboard, creating a more continuous surface for touch controls.

While the front frame and keycaps are made of plastic, the base and edges are metal. That combination gives the keyboard a familiar look for a Mac desk. As for the keyboard itself, it features a compact 78-key layout with scissor switches. You also get a fully functional row of function keys.

The Clevetura S is thicker than Apple’s Magic Keyboard, but it felt flatter under my hands when I first switched. I used the keyboard’s rear support to raise the incline, hoping to get closer to the typing angle I was used to. That tilted the keyboard a little too much for my liking. I wish there was a setting somewhere in between.
